text: Peter van Inwagen's 'Special Composition Question' asks:
choices: Under what conditions do some objects compose (become parts of) a further object?
Whether an object can survive the gradual replacement of all its parts over time.
Whether two distinct objects can occupy exactly the same place at the same time.
Whether every object is composed of mereological atoms or is infinitely divisible.
explanation: The Special Composition Question asks when some xs compose a y—the general conditions under which composition occurs. Distractor 2 is the coincidence problem and distractor 3 is the atomism-versus-gunk question; both are distinct mereological issues, not the SCQ itself.
